Summarize this text: Hey everyone, I hope you’re doing well. So, I’ve had a few days to think about this controversy on my own. Hopefully, by the time I post this comment things may’ve calmed down a bit, so I’d like to share my perspective on the matter. I understand that what I’m about to say might not be popular, and I’m prepared to accept the backlash I might recieve for it. However, I hope you hear me out.

We all know it’s frustrating when changes are made to a game we enjoy, and it’s natural to feel upset about it, specially when the changes are not of our liking. I empathize with all of you who feel irritated about it. However, I urge you to think twice before attributing these changes to some grand, sinister plan. Let’s focus on the fact that “They made changes I don’t like” is a valid reason to be upset, without jumping to assumptions about censorship. 

I say this because we’ve seen similar situations happen before. Companies make changes, people cry “censorship!!”, and warnings are raised about potential future censorships. But quite often, those warnings turn out to be false alarms. The cycle of anger lasts for a few days, and then we move on to the next outrage.

Now, I understand the passion for standing against censorship. It’s a valid stance, and one that I also support. However, what concerns me is when this particular situation, which some of you openly admit to having no interest in the game discussed, becomes just a platform for anti-censorship rhetoric. While I agree wholeheartedly with the principles of anti-censorship, I respectfully believe that this situation might not be the right battleground to fight that particular fight.
